mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month indicates economic weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% for 3 consecutive months) signals a potential for monetary easing, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows faster than the previous quarter and retail sales (RSAFS) also increase, it indicates strengthening economic demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances where both proxies show growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% in a month, coupled with a simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS), indicates inflationary pressures without real demand growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 2% in 1 month and RSAFS increases
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.
